CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFPROCRESULT

A stored procedure can return several result sets. Each CFPROCRESULT inside a CFSTOREDPROC turns one of them into an ordinary query variable that you can use with CFOUTPUT, CFLOOP and the query functions.

Category

Database manipulation

Syntax

<CFPROCRESULT NAME="query_name"
    RESULTSET="1-n"
    MAXROWS="maxrows">

Attributes

NAME
Required. Name of the query that receives the result set.
RESULTSET
Optional, default "1". Which result set to take, counting from 1.
MAXROWS
Optional. Maximum number of rows to keep.

Usage

As with CFPROCPARAM, KoldFusion parses the tag but never fills the query, because the enclosing CFSTOREDPROC always throws a Database exception on the flat-file driver. Test with IsDefined or IsQuery before using the result, or build it another way in your CFCATCH block.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFTRY>
  <CFSTOREDPROC PROCEDURE="sp_DeptReport" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
    <CFPROCRESULT NAME="Depts" RESULTSET="1">
    <CFPROCRESULT NAME="Courses" RESULTSET="2" MAXROWS="5">
  </CFSTOREDPROC>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Database">
    <P>No stored procedures on this driver. Running the two queries by hand instead.</P>
    <CFQUERY NAME="Depts" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
    SELECT Dept_Name, Location FROM Departments ORDER BY Dept_Name
    </CFQUERY>
    <CFQUERY NAME="Courses" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets" MAXROWS="5">
    SELECT CorName, CorLevel FROM CourseList ORDER BY CorName
    </CFQUERY>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>IsQuery(Depts): #IsQuery(Depts)#, IsQuery(Courses): #IsQuery(Courses)#</P>
</CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Department</TH><TH>Location</TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Depts"><TR><TD>#Dept_Name#</TD><TD>#Location#</TD></TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
<UL>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Courses"><LI>#CorName# (#CorLevel#)
</CFOUTPUT>
</UL>
